chunks: Where they will remain for aeons,

key_terms.أَحْقَابًا: aeons, long periods, or generations (plural of حِقْبَة)
key_terms.بِثِينَ: to remain or stay for a long time

ai.seo_question: How long will disbelievers remain in Hell according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the term 'ahqab' (plural of hubq) denotes a specific, extended period of time, often interpreted as a thousand years or a distinct epoch, underscoring the permanence of the abode of fire for the disbelievers. This verse is frequently cited to illustrate the severity of divine retribution for those who persist in kufr, contrasting with the temporary nature of purgatorial punishment for believers with minor sins. The emphasis on 'ahqab' serves as a theological anchor for the concept of eternal dwelling in Hell for those whose rejection of faith was absolute and unrepentant.
